title: Best Costco Dehumidifier (2026): Hisense, Midea and Danby
h1: The Best Costco Dehumidifiers — and How to Shop the Rotating Aisle
dek: Costco's dehumidifier selection comes and goes like everything else in the warehouse. Here's what's worth grabbing when you see it, and what to check before you do.
description: The best Costco dehumidifiers right now — the Hisense 35-pint plus rotating Midea and Danby 50-pint pump models — and how to judge a Costco deal before you buy.
intro: Shopping for a **Costco dehumidifier** is a little different from shopping on Amazon. Costco doesn't keep a fixed, searchable lineup; it runs a rotating assortment where models appear, sell through and sometimes return months later at a very different price. The only model we could confirm as a standing listing on Costco.com is the **Hisense 35-Pint (HD3526)**.

Beyond that, Midea and Danby 50-pint units with built-in pumps have shown up repeatedly in member deal reports during 2026, often in specific warehouses and sometimes for only a few weeks. That's great if you catch one at a clearance price — but it means you need to know what a good unit looks like before you're standing in the aisle. Here's what we found, which models are worth buying and what to check on the box.
topPicksLead: The **Hisense 35-Pint HD3526** is the best Costco dehumidifier you can reliably find: ENERGY STAR certified, sized for most rooms and consistently listed on Costco.com.

products.name: Hisense 35-Pint Dehumidifier (HD3526)
pros: Three fan speeds and 162 CFM airflow
Auto shut-off, washable filter, slide-out bucket
products.whyWeLoveIt: It's the one Costco dehumidifier you can count on finding, and it's a sensible, efficient machine for a large room or a mildly damp lower level. No treasure hunt required.
products.performance: Costco's item page lists it at 35 pints a day for up to 3,000 square feet, with ENERGY STAR certification, 162 CFM of airflow, three fan speeds and an 8.9-pint bucket that shuts the unit off when full. It has a washable filter and a slide-out tank, but no pump, so you'll be emptying the bucket unless you can set up gravity drainage. For a wet basement, our [basement picks](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/) have more capacity.

Check the model suffix on the box: an older MAD50PS1AWT-C version has also turned up, which can signal older clearance stock. Our [50-pint guide](/best/best-50-pint-dehumidifier/) compares it with rivals.

products.name: Danby 50-Pint Dehumidifier with Built-In Pump (DDR050BJPWDB)
products.award: Best if you catch it in stock
pros: Has appeared at steep clearance prices
cons: Danby has recall history on older models
products.whyWeLoveIt: When it's on the shelf, it's another capable 50-pint pump unit at a club price. It's a solid alternative to the Midea if that one isn't in your warehouse.
products.performance: This is a 50-pint compressor unit with a built-in pump for continuous drainage. Member reports showed it at a deep discount in spring 2026 before it went out of stock, so treat any price you see quoted online as stale until you check. Danby has been part of more than one CPSC recall on older models; read our [Danby guide](/best/best-danby-dehumidifier/) before buying, especially if you're considering a used or open-box unit.

blocks.text: That middle number is the key to shopping Costco. The same Midea pump model was reported at everything from roughly $100 on in-store clearance to about $200 at regular member price — the same box, months apart.

We don't lab-test dehumidifiers. For this guide we checked Costco.com for live listings and specs, tracked member-reported warehouse sightings and price history through 2026, and cross-checked each model's capacity and features against manufacturer information and the CPSC recall database.
We clearly separate the model you can order today from those you'll have to hunt for, and we judged each on capacity, drainage and safety history rather than on any single sale price.

sections.heading: What to look for in a Costco dehumidifier

items.label: The full model number
items.text: Check the suffix on the box. A different letter can mean older stock or a different version.

items.label: Capacity for your space
items.text: 35 pints for a large room, 50 pints for a basement. Our [size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) helps you decide.

items.label: A pump if you need one
items.text: If there's no floor drain near where it will sit, a built-in pump saves daily bucket trips. Compare options in our [pump guide](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/).

items.label: The manufacture date
items.text: On clearance or open-box units, check the nameplate date against CPSC.gov recalls.

items.label: Costco's return policy
items.text: Costco's generous returns are a real advantage for an appliance you can't try in the store. Keep the receipt.

sections.heading: Why Costco's dehumidifier selection keeps changing

blocks.text: Warehouse clubs work on a "treasure hunt" model: limited, rotating stock designed to make you buy when you see it. For dehumidifiers, that has a few practical consequences.

items: **Search won't always find it.** Costco.com reliably shows the Hisense HD3526, but the Midea and Danby pump units mostly surface through warehouse sightings and member forums.
**Prices are promotional and regional.** Member sales, in-store clearance and regional overstock all affect the same item number.
**Stock is a snapshot.** A unit that's gone today may reappear next season, and vice versa.

blocks.text: Not current stock, as far as we found. Midea's name is attached to a large 2016 CPSC recall — about 3.4 million 25- to 75-pint dehumidifiers built between 2003 and 2013 and sold under Midea, Frigidaire, Crosley, Kenmore and GE brands — but that's a different generation from the units now rotating through Costco. Danby has its own, separate recall history on older models. We found no CPSC dehumidifier recall for Hisense.

blocks.title: Buying used or deep clearance?
blocks.text: Find the manufacture date on the nameplate and check it at CPSC.gov. It takes two minutes and applies to any brand.

If you see a strong price at Costco on a model you've already researched, buy it — but don't wait around for it to come back. Sam's Club tends to have a shorter, steadier lineup; see our [Sam's Club guide](/best/best-sams-club-dehumidifier/). Walmart has the opposite problem, with a huge marketplace that mixes real brands with obscure imports; our [Walmart guide](/best/best-walmart-dehumidifier/) shows how to tell them apart.

A right-sized, honestly rated model from another retailer will serve you better than a mismatched bargain — our [best dehumidifier roundup](/best/best-dehumidifier/) is the place to start.

The **Hisense HD3526** is the best Costco dehumidifier you can reliably buy: efficient, right-sized for most rooms and always on Costco.com. If your warehouse has the **Midea 50-Pint with pump** or the **Danby 50-Pint with pump** at a good price, either is a smart grab for a basement — just check the model suffix and, for Danby, the recall history first.

faqs.a: Yes, but not as a fixed lineup. The Hisense 35-Pint HD3526 is a standing online listing; Midea and Danby 50-pint pump models rotate in and out of warehouses and Costco.com depending on season and region.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier at Costco?
faqs.a: For reliable availability, the Hisense HD3526: ENERGY STAR certified and rated for up to 3,000 square feet. For a basement, the Midea 50-Pint with built-in pump is the better find when it's in stock.

Sometimes. The Danby 50-pint with built-in pump (DDR050BJPWDB) has appeared at Costco during 2026, including at clearance prices, but it's frequently out of stock. Check Danby's recall history before buying, especially used or open-box.

faqs.q: Why do Costco dehumidifier prices vary so much?
faqs.a: Costco treats dehumidifiers as rotating seasonal deals. Member sales, in-store clearance and regional overstock can put the same model at very different prices within a few months.

faqs.q: Should I buy a dehumidifier at Costco or Amazon?
faqs.a: Buy at Costco if the specific model you want is in stock at a good price — the return policy is a plus. Amazon offers steadier availability and easier side-by-side comparison.
